expectations.text: Separates what goes to the authors, to the editor, and what is kept private
expectations.evidence: Sections 4/5/6 separate authors / editor / keep-private thoroughly.

expectations.text: Frames reuse/attribution/validation of established methods as the governing thesis for an integrated-platform paper (not a bug hunt)
expectations.evidence: Lists concerns with reproducibility as M1 and attribution as M3; does not frame reuse/attribution/validation as the governing thesis for an integrated platform.

expectations.text: Preserves confidentiality: warns against opening GitHub issues / contacting authors via the repo, and flags the journal AI-in-review policy
expectations.evidence: Section 6 says 'Do NOT open GitHub issues' and covers the AI-assistance policy.

expectations.text: Applies the 'reviewer is not the authors' QA' framing (bugs as evidence for the thesis, not a debugging service)
expectations.evidence: No 'reviewer is not the authors' QA' framing; treats findings as concerns to raise, not evidence-for-a-thesis.

expectations.text: Handles COI correctly: names the class of DEA tools and does not cite the reviewer's own package in the submittable text
expectations.evidence: Suggests benchmarking against 'limma, MSstats, DEqMS, proDA' and lists prolfqua among existing tools; no COI awareness.

expectations.text: Recommends a concise, thesis-first, human-voiced review (~750 words) rather than a five-page audit
expectations.evidence: Very long multi-section guidance doc; no conciseness/word-target guidance.
